name: Thailand-Cambodia border conflict
started: 2025-12-08 (second round of fighting; first round 24-28 Jul 2025)
summary: A century-old dispute over temples and a colonial-era border turned into two short wars in 2025, in July and again in December, when Thailand used F-16 air strikes and a ground offensive to take hills and temple sites claimed by Cambodia. A ceasefire signed on 27 December 2025 has held as a cold peace, with border crossings closed and occasional shooting incidents.
background: Both countries claim several temples and ridgelines along a border mapped by French colonial surveyors; the International Court of Justice awarded Preah Vihear temple to Cambodia in 1962 and clarified the ruling in 2013. Clashes in the Emerald Triangle in May 2025 escalated into five days of war in July 2025 that killed 43 people and displaced about 300,000 before a truce brokered with help from the United States, China and Malaysia.

On 26 October 2025 the two prime ministers signed the Kuala Lumpur Peace Accord, witnessed by Malaysia's Anwar Ibrahim and US President Donald Trump, covering heavy-weapons withdrawal, ASEAN observers, joint demining, temporary border markers, the release of 18 Cambodian prisoners and a joint task force against scam centres. It matters because the deal tied border peace to US trade arrangements, and its collapse showed how a single landmine can unravel high-level diplomacy.
year: On 10 November 2025 a landmine in Sisaket wounded two Thai soldiers (one lost a foot) and Thailand suspended the accord, saying the mine was newly laid; Cambodia said it was old. On 12 November Cambodia said Thai fire killed one civilian and wounded five at Prey Chan village. After a skirmish on 7 December, Thailand resumed ground operations and F-16 strikes on 8 December; Cambodia fired BM-21 rockets toward Buri Ram, and fighting spread around the Ta Muen Thom, Ta Krabey and Preah Vihear areas. On 10 December the Royal Thai Army launched Operation Sattawat and seized several areas inside Cambodia. Cambodia closed all border crossings on 13 December. Despite a ceasefire announcement by President Trump, fighting continued until a new ceasefire on 27 December with a 72-hour monitoring period; Thailand later released the 18 Cambodian soldiers captured in July. Thailand accused Cambodia of flying more than 250 drones into its territory on 29 December.

In 2026 the truce held, though Thailand accused Cambodia of firing a 40 mm grenade near a Thai patrol in Sisaket on 24 February. The ceasefire was still in effect as of May 2026, amid mistrust and sporadic incidents.
situation: As of late October 2026 the front is quiet but militarised. Thai forces hold the temples and hills taken in December 2025 (Ta Krabey, Khana, Ta Muen Thom, Chong An Ma, at least five hills and parts of O Smach and Thmor Da per Wikipedia's compilation), while Cambodia holds parts of the Emerald Triangle, Hill 745 and the Preah Vihear promontory. Border crossings remain largely closed. No sourced fatal clash after the ceasefire was found for 2026.
technical: 8 Dec 2025: Thai army began 'using aircraft to strike military targets in several areas'; Wikipedia records F-16 strikes on multiple positions inside Cambodia (Ittefaq/AFP; Wikipedia).
Cambodia fired BM-21 multiple rockets toward Buri Ram province on 8 Dec 2025 (no casualties reported) (Ittefaq/AFP).
Cambodia said Thai tanks fired on Tamone Thom (Ta Muen Thom) temple and areas near Preah Vihear temple on 8 Dec 2025 (Ittefaq/AFP).
Operation Sattawat (from 10 Dec 2025): Royal Thai Army ground offensive that seized localities in northern Cambodia (Wikipedia).
7 Dec 2025 skirmish: Cambodia says Thai troops used small arms, B-40 grenades and 60 mm mortars at Prolean Thmor, Choam Khsant District, Preah Vihear (Wikipedia).
Mines found by Thai units in Oct 2025: PMN-2, POMZ-2 and MN-79 types (Wikipedia).
Air defence: RTAF signed a $108 million deal for the Barak MX system in early Dec 2025 (Wikipedia).
Drones: Thailand alleged 250+ Cambodian drones crossed into Thailand on 29 Dec 2025, a day after the ceasefire (Wikipedia).
July 2025 round context: Royal Thai Navy task force of four vessels near Ko Kut and Ban Hat Lek (Wikipedia).
Ceasefire mechanism: 72-hour monitoring period after 27 Dec 2025; the KL accord's interim ASEAN observer team was part of the suspended October deal (Wikipedia).
casualties: July 2025 round: 43 killed (AFP via Ittefaq). December 2025 round: no consolidated, sourced toll retrieved; one Thai soldier killed and four wounded on 8 Dec alone (Thai army via AFP). Wikipedia's whole-conflict infobox carries contested, inconsistently attributed figures (an OSINT estimate of 73 to 160+ Cambodian military and border police killed, a claim of about 505 soldiers killed with 6 to 13 T-55 tanks destroyed, and a separate figure of 42 soldiers killed and 531+ injured) that should be treated as unverified.
displaced: About 35,000 evacuated in Thailand by 8 Dec 2025 (Thai Second Army Region via AFP); July 2025 round displaced about 300,000 (AFP). No sourced December 2025 total retrieved.

timeline.event: Kuala Lumpur Peace Accord signed by Anutin and Hun Manet, witnessed by Anwar and Trump.
Landmine wounds two Thai soldiers in Sisaket; Thailand suspends the accord.
Cambodia says Thai fire kills one civilian at Prey Chan.
Thailand resumes ground operations and F-16 strikes; Cambodia fires BM-21 rockets.
Royal Thai Army launches Operation Sattawat.
Thailand alleges 250+ Cambodian drones crossed its border.
Thai army reports Cambodian 40 mm grenade fire near a Sisaket patrol.

outlook: Watch whether the two sides resume joint boundary commission work and demining, whether crossings reopen to trade, and whether Thailand hands back any positions taken in December. A landmine casualty or a shooting at a temple site could again unravel the truce.

zones.name: Ta Muen Thom and Ta Krabey temples (Surin-Oddar Meanchey)
zones.note: Temple complexes taken by Thai forces in Dec 2025.

zones.name: Preah Vihear and Phu Makhuea (Sisaket-Preah Vihear)
zones.note: Preah Vihear temple awarded to Cambodia by ICJ; heavy fighting in both rounds.

zones.name: Chong An Ma and Emerald Triangle (Ubon Ratchathani)
zones.note: Site of May 2025 clash; Thai hold Chong An Ma, Cambodia parts of the Emerald Triangle (approximate).

zones.name: O Smach (Oddar Meanchey)
zones.note: Border town partially occupied by Thai forces in Dec 2025 (approximate).

zones.name: Ban Nong Chan and Prey Chan (Sa Kaeo-Banteay Meanchey)
zones.note: Disputed villages; Thai mine clearance and Nov 2025 shooting (approximate).

zones.name: Thmor Da and Trat coast
zones.note: Thmor Da area partially occupied by Thai forces; Thai naval actions near Ko Kut in July 2025 (approximate).

battles.name: December 2025 Thai-Cambodian border war (Operation Sattawat)
battles.place: Ta Muen Thom, Ta Krabey and Preah Vihear sectors, Thailand-Cambodia border
battles.outcome: Thai forces took temple sites (Ta Krabey, Khana, Ta Muen Thom), Chong An Ma, at least five hills and parts of O Smach and Thmor Da before a ceasefire on 27 Dec 2025 (per Wikipedia compilation).
battles.forces: Thai F-16 strikes, tanks and Second Army Region ground forces in Operation Sattawat; Cambodian BM-21 rockets, mortars and small arms.
battles.losses: One Thai soldier killed and four wounded on 8 Dec (Thai army via AFP); no consolidated sourced toll retrieved for the full round. About 35,000 Thais evacuated by 8 Dec.
battles.significance: The second war in five months broke a US-witnessed peace accord and left Thailand holding disputed ground, setting the terms of the current cold peace.
